title: Recover an FSM from a Flattened Sequential Netlist
description: Reverse-engineer a flattened gate-level synchronous sequential netlist into clean, word-level, behaviorally equivalent Verilog RTL.

ports.name: in
ports.description: single-bit control input sampled on rising clk edges

ports.name: out
ports.description: single-bit Moore output reflecting current state

interface.signature: module recovered_fsm(input clk, input rst, input in, output out);

metrics.name: functional_equivalence
metrics.description: Fraction of evaluator-generated stimulus sequences (shipped + hidden random + adversarial) for which recovered_fsm's out waveform exactly matches the reference flattened_netlist.v simulation, cycle by cycle, via iverilog/vvp simulation.

metrics.name: word_recovery_rate
metrics.description: Whether the submission expresses the FSM using word-level behavioral RTL (state register(s), always block, case/if-based transition logic) rather than gate-primitive instantiation.

metrics.name: structural_match_accuracy
metrics.description: Interface conformance score: correctness of module name 'recovered_fsm' and exact port list (clk, rst, in, out with correct directions/widths).

metrics.name: compile_success
metrics.description: Whether iverilog successfully compiles submission/recovered_rtl.v together with the generated testbench with zero errors.

constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; submit only submission/recovered_rtl.v.
The submitted file must be self-contained (single module, no external includes).
Do not instantiate or reference any gate-level primitive modules from primitives.v; the recovered design must be written at the word/register level.
The module must use a single clock domain and a synchronous active-high reset.
